goal: I am an integration tester. I need to design integration tests for the user registration functionality. Before defining the tests, I need to understand the high-level architecture supporting this functionality. I want to identify the main components involved in the registration process, their responsibilities, and the interactions and dependencies among them. In particular, I need to understand which components handle the registration request, validate the user's personal information and selected role, manage role-specific data such as the student ID or librarian identifier, verify the validity and uniqueness of the account, and persist the newly created user. I also need to understand how these components collaborate when invalid or already existing user data is provided, so that I can identify the main integration points and interactions that should be covered by the tests.

views.title: Decomposition view — user registration functionality
views.purpose: Shows the main components of user registration, grouped by layer, with the responsibility each takes in the registration request, validation, role-specific data, uniqueness checks and persistence.

elements.name: AuthenticationController
responsibilities: exposes the POST /api/auth/register endpoint
forwards role, name, surname, email, password and identifier to LibraryFacade

elements.name: Registration
responsibilities: collects the registration form fields and the selected role in the Swing client
requires all fields to be filled before calling LibraryFacade
shows the error message of a failed registration

elements.name: RestExceptionHandler
responsibilities: maps IllegalArgumentException to an HTTP 400 response carrying the error message

elements.name: LibraryFacade
responsibilities: single entry point that delegates register to UserManager

elements.name: UserManager
responsibilities: validates the role, the first name and the password length before anything else
validates first name, last name, email and identifier of a student or librarian
selects StudentFactory or LibrarianFactory according to the role
checks the student ID format (uppercase letter followed by 8 digits)
rejects an email already associated with an account
rejects an identifier already in use
raises a server error when the user could not be saved

elements.name: UserFactory
responsibilities: declares createUser(name, surname, email, password, identifier) for role-specific users

elements.name: StudentFactory
responsibilities: creates a Student whose studentNumber is the identifier

elements.name: LibrarianFactory
responsibilities: creates a Librarian whose internalIdentifierCode is the identifier

elements.name: Student
responsibilities: holds the unique studentNumber of a student

elements.name: Librarian
responsibilities: holds the unique internalIdentifierCode of a librarian

elements.name: UserRegistry
responsibilities: looks up users by institutional email, student number and librarian code
saves a newly created user through PersistenceManager

elements.name: User
responsibilities: abstract base entity of Student and Librarian with a unique institutionalEmail

elements.name: PersistenceManager
responsibilities: persists an entity in a transaction and returns false after a rollback
finds the first entity matching field values

elements.name: JpaUtil
responsibilities: creates EntityManager instances from the reservationsPU persistence unit

limitations: Layer groups are containers and are not counted toward the 15-element cap; the 14 drawn components fit the cap.
is-part-of is drawn as nesting of each component in its layer group (the relations are listed in view.json).
UserDTO (returned by AuthenticationController, LibraryFacade and UserManager) is not an element of the evidence model and is not drawn.

limitations: RestExceptionHandler has no relation: Spring binds it through @RestControllerAdvice/@ExceptionHandler, so no registration component depends on it statically. Its role in failure paths is shown in V3.
Generalization (StudentFactory/LibrarianFactory implement UserFactory; Student/Librarian extend User) is not a Client-Server relation kind and is not drawn; it is in the evidence model.
Swing Registration calls LibraryFacade in-process; the only request-reply connector (HTTP from registration.html to AuthenticationController) is shown in V3.
The 15-element cap is reached (14 components and the datastore); layer groups are containers and not counted.
UserDTO is not drawn (not an element of the evidence model).

limitations: One scenario only: registration through POST /api/auth/register. The Swing client calls LibraryFacade.register directly and shows errors with showError(ex.getMessage()); it is an alternative entry and is not drawn.
The returns '400 {error}', 'UserDTO' and the RuntimeException of a failed save are inferred from the controller/handler/manager code (no direct call), so they have support 'inferred'.

RestExceptionHandler handles IllegalArgumentException, IllegalStateException and SecurityException only: the RuntimeException of a failed save has no handler in the code, so the HTTP response of that path is not evidenced.
Role alternatives (Student / Librarian) are drawn as alt/else pairs of the fragments recorded separately in the evidence model.
The layered overlay is shown as stereotypes on the lifelines (lifelines follow first appearance, so layer boxes cannot be contiguous).
